name: Rivaroxaban
route_note: oral tablet, once daily for AF (with food at higher doses); twice daily initially for VTE; oral suspension for children
owner: Bayer; Janssen (Johnson & Johnson) in the US

discovery.note: An oxazolidinone-based direct factor Xa inhibitor discovered by Bayer in the late 1990s. Year is the priority date of Bayer's patent application on substituted oxazolidinones (WO 01/47919).

tagline: The first oral direct factor Xa inhibitor to reach the market
summary: Rivaroxaban is an oral anticoagulant that directly inhibits factor Xa. It is used for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation, for treatment and prevention of venous thromboembolism, and at low dose with aspirin in chronic coronary or peripheral artery disease.
mechanism: Rivaroxaban binds reversibly to the active site of free and clot-bound factor Xa and of the prothrombinase complex, independent of antithrombin.
Inhibiting factor Xa interrupts both intrinsic and extrinsic pathways and reduces thrombin generation. Andexanet alfa or prothrombin complex concentrate can reverse it.
uses: Stroke prevention in non-valvular atrial fibrillation
Treatment and secondary prevention of DVT and PE
VTE prophylaxis after hip or knee replacement and in medically ill patients
Reduction of major cardiovascular events in chronic CAD or PAD (2.5 mg twice daily with aspirin)

history.title: First approvals
history.detail: Approved in the EU and Canada for VTE prevention after hip or knee replacement.

history.title: ROCKET AF and FDA
history.detail: ROCKET AF shows non-inferiority to warfarin in AF; the FDA approves Xarelto in July for orthopaedic prophylaxis and in November for AF.

history.title: COMPASS
history.detail: Low-dose rivaroxaban plus aspirin reduces cardiovascular events in stable atherosclerotic disease.

history.title: Vascular indication
history.detail: FDA approves the 2.5 mg dose for chronic CAD/PAD.

history.title: Paediatric use
history.detail: FDA approves rivaroxaban for VTE treatment in children.

pk.bioavailability: ~80–100% at 10 mg; higher doses need food
pk.metabolism: CYP3A4/2J2 and CYP-independent hydrolysis; P-gp substrate

safety.boxed_warning: Premature discontinuation increases the risk of thrombotic events; spinal/epidural haematoma may occur with neuraxial anaesthesia or spinal puncture.

facts: Increased thrombotic events in triple-positive antiphospholipid syndrome were seen in the TRAPS trial.
It is developed and marketed jointly by Bayer and Janssen.

references.title: Patel MR et al. Rivaroxaban versus warfarin in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (ROCKET AF). N Engl J Med 2011
